source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (Payment Systems Report)
why_relevant: Annual regulator report with POS terminal counts, acceptance-point growth, acquirer market concentration and instant-payment/qvik adoption — the quantitative baseline against which vendor claims and partnership announcements are calibrated.

source_name: GVH sectoral inquiry into the card-acceptance market
why_relevant: Hungarian Competition Authority's deep-dive into the acquiring market names the acquirers, their shares, contract structures and terminal economics — rare, evidence-grade competitor intelligence unavailable from vendors.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. — instant payment / qvik / fizetési kérelem service pages
why_relevant: GIRO operates the Hungarian instant payment system and qvik; it publishes the list of payment service providers offering fizetési kérelem/GIROInstant — an authoritative, machine-readable partner/participant roster and a leading indicator of who is live with qvik acceptance.

source_name: Ecommerce Hungary (SzEK.org) — trade association
why_relevant: 200+ member association spanning merchants, banks, PSPs, logistics and technology vendors; membership lists, Trustmark scheme and conference (EkerNap) programmes reveal which acquirers/PSPs court Hungarian merchants and with whom they co-present case studies.

source_name: Kosárérték.hu — Hungarian e-commerce trade portal, company profiles
why_relevant: E-commerce trade media with per-company profile pages for payment providers (e.g. Worldline) and coverage of association initiatives; good for merchant-side perception, case studies and partnership news.

source_name: Nevogate / paymentgateway.hu partner integration directory
why_relevant: A Hungarian payment-gateway aggregator listing which acquirers and payment methods it integrates (Worldline/SIX, PayU, SEPA DD, etc.) — an indirect but concrete map of who is technically connectable in the HU market.

source_name: K&H Bank qvik / payment-request merchant documentation
why_relevant: K&H publishes merchant-facing qvik/fizetési kérelem documentation showing how a bank acquirer operationalises instant payment acceptance; comparable documents from OTP and MBH allow bank-by-bank capability benchmarking.

source_name: Hungarian company registries (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN, Céginfo)
why_relevant: Entity resolution and ownership/financial baseline for HU PSPs and acquirers (legal names, tax numbers, shareholders, filed accounts) — necessary to link brand names (Barion, SimplePay, Wise HU branch) to legal entities and to detect ownership changes.

source_name: Shopify App Store — SimplePay (by OTP Mobil) listing
why_relevant: Marketplace listings expose distribution strategy, supported markets, install/review counts and release notes for HU PSPs — an indirect quantitative proxy for merchant adoption that vendors do not publish.

source_name: Shoprenter / Számlázz.hu integration directories
why_relevant: Dominant Hungarian webshop and invoicing platforms publish which PSPs are integrated; their directories and blog guides are a bottom-up census of which acquirers/PSPs actually reach Hungarian SME merchants.

source_name: ACI Worldwide Investor Relations — News Releases
why_relevant: ACI has issued named Hungarian customer announcements: OTP Bank Group (UP Retail Payments, UP Payments Risk Management, API Manager, UP Immediate Payments) and a release stating ACI plus partners Capsys and T-Systems power the majority (~75%) of Hungary's real-time payments, naming OTP, Erste Bank Hungary and Takarekinfo. This is a rare public confirmation of core payment-hub suppliers to Hungarian banks and of the local system-integrator layer.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide GCS press-release mirror
why_relevant: Second IR host carrying older Euronet releases (ABN AMRO Hungary, Bank Austria Creditanstalt, CEE peers) that do not all surface on the primary IR domain; useful for reconstructing the historical HU ATM outsourcing timeline.

source_name: Finastra Press & Media
why_relevant: Carries a 2026 release in which Raiffeisen Bank (RBI group, Hungary among the covered markets) reaffirms Finastra as the platform powering its core retail services — direct named-client confirmation of a core-banking supplier relationship touching Hungary. The paginated archive is a standing feed for further CEE/HU named clients.

source_name: Temenos Press Releases / News
why_relevant: Temenos systematically publishes 'X bank selects/goes live on Temenos' releases; the archive is the canonical way to detect any Hungarian core-banking win. No HU-named release surfaced in this pass, so treat as a monitoring feed rather than a confirmed HU source.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Banking Case Studies hub
why_relevant: Global named-customer case-study library (Valiant, FOREX, Sparkasse Hannover, CSOB and other European banks) published as downloadable PDFs. No Hungarian client case study located in this pass, but the hub is the single best place a HU reference would appear, and the CEE entries map competitor footprint next door.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf investor press-release CDN archive (q4cdn)
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf's IR document store holds the raw press-release files (e.g. bank99 ATM-as-a-Service, 2025 awards). Contract announcements naming a Hungarian bank would land here; the file store is easier to sweep than the marketing site.

source_name: NCR Atleos Newsroom
why_relevant: NCR/Atleos runs its largest global ATM manufacturing plant in Budapest (350,000th ATM milestone release, 750+ employees) — a HU industrial footprint fact confirmed by the vendor itself — and the newsroom is where any HU bank ATM/ATMaaS win would be announced. Ownership is in flux (Brink's acquisition reported 2026), so releases also track supplier-structure change.

source_name: NCR Voyix Newsroom
why_relevant: Post-split sibling of Atleos covering retail/digital banking software; needed to disambiguate which legal entity holds a Hungarian bank or retail relationship after the 2023 separation.

source_name: Finextra press-release wire (vendor-submitted)
why_relevant: Vendors submit their customer-win releases to Finextra verbatim, so it mirrors HU-naming announcements (e.g. OTP Bank–ACI instant payments) even when the vendor site reorganises or removes them. Good redundancy layer and searchable by bank name.

source_name: Business Wire — vendor releases naming Hungarian banks
why_relevant: Primary distribution copy of vendor announcements (ACI + Capsys + T-Systems / Hungary real-time payments). Authoritative dated text, stable URLs, and a searchable index across all payment vendors.

source_name: FeaturedCustomers — vendor customer-reference aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates published customer references, testimonials and case studies per vendor (Diebold Nixdorf profile seen with 39 references). Fast way to enumerate a vendor's named install base and spot any Hungarian entity without crawling each vendor site.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer database — ACI Worldwide BASE24
why_relevant: Lists named institutions running a specific payment product (BASE24), broken out by country. A cheap way to hypothesise which Hungarian banks run ACI switching before confirming against vendor press releases.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — Diebold Nixdorf company showcase (news + resources)
why_relevant: Vendor-sponsored showcase pages republish ATM vendor case studies, white papers and deployment news in one place, including NCR/Atleos corporate-structure coverage. Useful pointer into vendor collateral that is otherwise buried behind gated resource centres.

source_name: Thales Cyber & Digital (cpl.thalesgroup.com) — payment HSM resources
why_relevant: payShield product and resource pages carry integration guides, partner listings and occasional named case studies; the partner/integration lists are the realistic route to identifying who supplies HSMs into Hungarian issuers and processors, since Thales rarely names individual banks.

source_name: Capsys Kft. — Hungarian banking systems integrator (vendor-side reference source)
source_subtype: company registry entry / local integrator profile (pointer to corporate site)
why_relevant: Capsys is named by ACI as a delivery partner for Hungary's instant-payment (azonnali fizetés / AFR) rollout and is reported to have designed and implemented AFR for two major Hungarian banks and, with T-Systems Magyarország, for the Takarék group. Local integrators are often the only public trace linking an international platform to a specific Hungarian bank.

source_name: IBS Intelligence / Electronic Payments International / fintechfutures — vendor-win trade coverage
why_relevant: Specialist banking-tech trade titles restate vendor customer wins with added context and sometimes name banks the vendor release only alludes to (e.g. ACI's HU real-time share; OTP picking ACI for open banking). Good corroboration layer and a discovery channel for older deals.

source_name: The Paypers / thepaypers.com — vendor-selection news naming Hungarian banks
why_relevant: Publishes 'bank X selects vendor Y' items for Hungary specifically (Erste Bank Hungary selecting valantic for request-to-pay), which widens the vendor map beyond the original eleven-vendor list and confirms adjacent supplier relationships.

source_name: MindSpire — Hungarian core-banking selection/transformation blog (banki transzformáció)
why_relevant: Hungarian consultancy writing in Hungarian about packaged core-banking system selection, citing Hungarian bank transformation examples (e.g. Erste). Local-language consultancy content often names the vendor shortlists and incumbents that international vendors do not publish.
